**Finding submitted: INDEMN — missing (critical), preferred level.**

**What I found**

- The Agreement has **no indemnity clause at all**. Numbering jumps from § 19.5 (`p0075`) directly to the § 21 limitation-of-liability heading (`p0076`) — Section 20 is entirely absent. Searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless", "defend", "infringe", "third-party claim" and "losses/expenses/attorneys' fees" surfaced no operative indemnity.
- What survives are four clauses that **presuppose** an indemnity that isn't there:
  - § 9.3 — termination right keyed to "the remedies required by **Section 20.5**" (dangling);
  - § 19.4 — remedy is non-exclusive for "indemnified claims";
  - § 21.3 — "its **indemnification obligations**" is an Excluded Claim (i.e. uncapped);
  - § 30.5 — preserves enforcement rights of "an indemnified party" and "vested indemnity rights".
- This sits in **walk-away territory** (no Vendor IP indemnity). There is also no Customer indemnity anywhere, so nothing one-sided to narrow.

**What I proposed** — one `insert_after` § 19.5 creating Section 20: Vendor defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer **and its Affiliates** against third-party claims for (a) IP infringement/misappropriation by the Services or Deliverables, (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law, (c) unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct; plus notice, control of the defence and reasonable cooperation; and any Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

**Why preferred, not fallback** — the fallback would have us volunteer a 3× annual-fees super-cap on Vendor's indemnity, when § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as **uncapped** Excluded Claims. Conceding a cap where none exists would be adverse to us, so the fallback's cap and its procure/modify/replace/refund mechanics are left for negotiation rather than drafted in. All ten preferred elements are carried by the single inserted clause; the only residual point is housekeeping — § 9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" should be conformed to the new Section 20, which I flagged in the comment rather than treating as a substantive gap.
